headlines.title: Janus Electric targets $65M North America revenue
headlines.summary:
Janus Electric CEO and managing director Ben Hutt talked with Proactive about the company’s latest operational and funding developments, including its North American order book, investment from battery partner Electrovaya and the rollout of its Horizon Two strategy.

Janus has strengthened its ability to execute on its delivery plans after arranging a working capital facility with Commonwealth Bank and securing a A$2 million strategic investment from Electrovaya. He said the funding arrangements would help support the company’s supply chain, inventory requirements and delivery schedule for customers in North America.

The company has placed initial battery orders worth around A$37.5 million, which Hutt explained would be drawn down in stages rather than committed all at once. He said the arrangement gave Janus Electric greater certainty around delivery timing for customers in California and Canada.

Janus Electric’s North American order book currently stands at 124 trucks. Hutt said the company had reaffirmed its expectation of delivering the published North American order book by early in the fourth quarter, targeting the end of April. The associated disclosed revenue is around A$64.5 million to A$65 million.

Hutt also discussed Horizon Two, including expansion across five US regions, conversion capacity in Los Angeles and Texas, and the proposed RANGER joint venture in Western Australia. He said the company remained focused on execution, building its team and putting converted electric trucks equipped with new batteries onto the road.

Looking further ahead, Hutt said Janus Electric’s strategy was aimed at scaling to 600 trucks on the road in its next phase, with a longer-term ambition of reaching 2,000 trucks.

headlines.title: Money 20/20 USA: Hopper’s Adi Soloducho on Closing the Cardholder Loyalty Gap
headlines.summary: Premium cardholders are paying more for their cards and expecting more in return, but many feel their rewards aren’t keeping up. Adi Soloducho, VP of Product, Corporate and Enterprise Commerce at Hopper Technology Solutions, sits down with JD Durkin at Money 20/20 USA in Las Vegas to unpack what she calls the “loyalty gap” and why travel, not cash back, is how banks can close it. Soloducho explains how the business behind the popular Hopper app now powers travel for banks around the world, including RBC’s Avion Rewards, Canada’s largest proprietary loyalty program, and Nubank’s NuViagens in Latin America and CommBank in Australia. She walks through how card programs are climbing a ladder from airline partnerships to platforms to full ecosystems, why embedded protections like Cancel for Any Reason and Disruption Assistance matter to both banks and travelers, and where loyalty in banking is headed next.
